name: 05-fidelity
title: Mechanistic Fidelity — agreement, discrepancy, and missing physiology
question:
The capability studies show the same spec running under interchangeable engines.
But do the engines actually agree, and where do they diverge? This is the honest
backbone. The demonstration is credible only if the engines' limits are measured,
not hidden.
objective:
Establish where the BioGears C++ engine and the exact SBML extraction agree
(baseline, inflammation core) and where they diverge (the hemodynamic layer). Map
each divergence to the BioGears subsystem the extraction omits, so the
"same spec, many engines" claim is shown with its limits stated.
claim:
The engines agree where the extraction is faithful and diverge where it is not. At
rest both hold the StandardMale baseline. Under infection the inflammation core
(tissue integrity, blood pathogen) matches to within ~0.1% in both the mild and
severe arms. They diverge in the hemodynamic layer. The engine fluctuates
continuously (from its nutrition schedule and full homeostatic control) while the
autonomous extraction is near-flat. Under severe sepsis both reach MAP<65 shock, but
by opposite mechanisms and in flipped order: the engine by a hypodynamic low-output
route (MAP<65 at 69.3 h), the extraction by a hyperdynamic vasodilatory route (MAP<65
at 54.1 h) — ~15 h earlier, even though it lags ~11 h on systolic pressure. Every
divergence maps to a vasomotor, fluid, or metabolic subsystem the extraction omits
(nitric oxide, fever vasodilation, renal fluid handling, lactate, intracellular
water). The surrogate is a further, coarser approximation (study 04): fast, bounded,
not clinically accurate.

expected_behavior.statement: Baseline and the inflammation core agree to within ~0.1%; the hemodynamic layer diverges in mechanism and timing, mapped to omitted subsystems.

findings.summary: Where they agree — baseline parity and a near-identical (~0.1%) inflammation core.
findings.detail:
At rest both engines hold the StandardMale baseline within tolerance
(00_baseline_parity). Under infection the inflammation observables match to ~0.1%
in both the mild and severe arms (02_inflammation_match): tissue integrity (min
0.243/0.243 severe) and blood pathogen (peak 330.2/330.6). The extracted Acute
Inflammatory Response is a faithful translation of the engine's.

findings.summary: Where they diverge — the hemodynamic layer, in mechanism and timing.
findings.detail:
The divergence lives entirely in the hemodynamics (01_divergence_heatmap). The
engine fluctuates continuously while the autonomous extraction is near-flat. Under
severe sepsis the two reach MAP<65 shock by opposite routes and in flipped order
(engine hypodynamic, MAP<65 at 69.3 h; extraction hyperdynamic, MAP<65 at 54.1 h).
The functional-difference matrix (03_functional_difference_matrix) maps every
divergence to the BioGears subsystem the extraction omits or leaves inert (nitric
oxide, fever vasodilation, renal/urine, lactate, intracellular water).
findings.statement: The hemodynamic divergence is not transcription noise. It is two internally consistent, opposite shock trajectories: the engine reaches MAP<65 by a hypodynamic low-output route (69.3 h), the extraction by a hyperdynamic vasodilatory route (54.1 h). The ~15 h timing gap — earlier even though the extraction lags ~11 h on systolic pressure — and the engine's continuous fluctuation against the extraction's near-flat profile both point to the vasomotor, fluid, and metabolic subsystems the extraction omits, not to a faithfulness failure in the shared spec.
findings.explanation:
Agreement on the inflammation core to within ~0.1% (tissue integrity, blood pathogen) bounds the extraction's error to the hemodynamic layer. The acute inflammatory response is a faithful translation of the engine's; the closed-loop cardiovascular control is not. That turns the divergence into a testable disagreement. The two engines make different predictions about the same severe patient. The C++ engine predicts low-output shock: output falls and MAP<65 arrives later, at 69.3 h. The extraction predicts vasodilatory shock: peripheral resistance falls and MAP<65 arrives earlier, at 54.1 h, even though its systolic pressure trails by ~11 h. Both cannot be right about the real trajectory, so at least one route is an artifact of what the model carries, and every mapped divergence traces to a subsystem the extraction leaves out or inert (nitric oxide, fever vasodilation, renal/urine fluid handling, lactate, intracellular water).

This leaves one test open: trace the cardiac-output-versus-systemic-vascular-resistance split through the shock crossing across the severity sweep and compare it against the BioGears C++ reference. The engine whose output-vs-resistance partition matches the reference at MAP<65 is the faithful one; the other's shock route is the artifact. On the committed severe runs alone, this study measures that the engines diverge and maps each divergence to an omitted subsystem, but it does not yet settle which shock trajectory is correct. The study-04 surrogate is a further, coarser approximation on top of the extraction. The divergence is real and subsystem-localised; which of the two routes is right is still open.
